rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good things are those that sound, cultivated natures do not find repugnant.
rows.anchor: أحل لكم الطيبات} وهي ما لم تستخبثه الطباع السليمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, good things are those no revealed text or juristic analogy establishes as forbidden.
rows.anchor: أو ما لم يدل نص شارع ولا قياس مجتهد على حرمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food of the People of the Book means Jews and Christians and includes their slaughtered meat as well as other food.
rows.anchor: اليهود والنصارى والمراد بطعامهم ما يتناول ذبائحهم وغيرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عامة التابعين، أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas allowed slaughter by Arab Christians; this was also the general Successor position and the view adopted by Abu Hanifa and his companions.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه سئل عن ذبائح نصارى العرب فقال : لا بأس وهو قول عامة التابعين وبه أخذ أبو حنيفة وأصحابه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa treats the Sabians as People of the Book.
rows.anchor: وحكم الصابئين حكم أهل الكتاب عنده

rows.speaker: صاحباه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions divide the Sabians into Psalm readers who worship angels and scriptureless star worshippers; the latter are not People of the Book.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحباه هما صنفان : صنف يقرأون الزبور ويعبدون الملائكة وصنف لا يقرأون كتابا ويعبدون النجوم فهؤلاء ليسوا من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magians receive the People of the Book's jizya treatment, but their slaughtered meat and women are excluded, on the cited Prophetic instruction.
rows.anchor: سنوا بهم سنة أهل الكتاب غير ناكحي نسائهم ولا آكلي ذبائحهم

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
rows.claim: Most scholars permit meat slaughtered by a Jew or Christian in another name, such as Christ's, because God permitted their slaughter knowing what they say.
rows.anchor: فذهب أكثر أهل العلم إلى أنه يحل فإن الله قد أحل ذبائحهم وهو يعلم ما يقولون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan forbids eating if one hears a Jew or Christian invoke another name, but permits it if one did not hear, since their slaughter is allowed.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن إذا ذبح اليهودي أو النصراني فذكر اسم غير الله وأنت تسمع فلا تأكله وإذا غاب عنك فكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims may feed and sell their food to People of the Book; otherwise the verse's reciprocal permission would not make sense.
rows.anchor: فلا عليكم أن تطعموهم وتبيعوه منهم ولو حرم عليهم لم يجز ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believing women specified are free and chaste; mentioning them encourages the preferable choice without excluding Muslim slave women or non-chaste women, whose marriages are valid by consensus.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهن الحرائر والعفائف وتخصيصهن بالذكر للبعث على ما هو الأولى لا لنفي ما عداهن فإن نكاح الإماء المسلمات صحيح بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة، الشافعي
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa treats enslaved women from the Book as he treats Muslim slave women, while al-Shafi‘i disagrees.
rows.anchor: وأما الإماء الكتابيات فهن كالمسلمات عند أبي حنيفة خلافا للشافعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas holds that women from the People of the Book who are at war are not lawful to marry.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : لا تحل الحربيات

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi reports that some jurists infer the verse forbids marrying an enslaved woman from the Book, but the author says the sound view permits it.
rows.anchor: قال الحدادي واستدل بعض الفقهاء بظاهر الآية على أنه لا يجوز للمسلم نكاح الأمة الكتابية والصحيح أنه يجوز

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Jews asked about his religion, the Prophet affirmed belief in God and all revelations; after he mentioned Jesus, they disparaged the Muslims' worldly and religious standing, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن نفرا من اليهود سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To resent someone means to fault, reject, or dislike something about them; here the question asks what defect the Jews find in the Muslims' religion.
rows.anchor: من نقم منه كذا إذا عابه وأنكره وكرهه أي ما تعيبون وما تنكرون منا ديننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The only alleged cause for resentment is that Muslims believe in God and the revelations sent to them and before them, including the Quran, Torah, Gospel, and other divine books.
rows.anchor: إلا لأن آمنا بالله فهو مفعول له لتنقمون على حذف المفعول به الذي هو الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of the Jews are called defiantly sinful because they rebel against faith in these revelations; if they believed their own scripture confirming the Quran, they would accept it.
rows.anchor: حتى لو كنتم مؤمنين بكتابكم الناطق بصحة كتابنا لآمنتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although all are sinful, the verse says most because those leading the others into rebellion and corruption bear the active responsibility.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الفسق إلى أكثرهم مع أن كلهم فاسقون لأنهم الحاملون لأعقابهم على التمرد والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate parsing attaches the clause to the belief phrase as an object: what the Jews dislike is belief in all revealed books and the Muslims' contrary stance toward them.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو عطف على أن آمنا على أنه مفعول به لكن لا على أن المستثنى مجموع المعطوفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses the Jews and asks whether they should be told what is truly worse than the faith they condemn; Islam itself contains no evil, so the wording signals absolute excess.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى المنقوم وهو الإيمان والمنقوم منهم المؤمنون أي هل أخبركم بما هو شر في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says Islam has certainly no evil, so “worse” means an absolute increase rather than a comparison with Islam.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : ومن المعلوم قطعا أنه لا شر في دين الإسلام فالمراد الزيادة المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for recompense normally denotes reward, paired with punishment for evil; it is used ironically here and is parsed as an accusative of specification.
rows.anchor: والمثوبة مختصة بالخير كالعقوبة مختصة بالشر فوضعت ههنا موضعها على طريق التهكم ونصبها على التمييز من بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cursed one is the implied subject's religion, meaning the Jews, whom God removed from mercy and condemned for disbelief and persistent sin after clear signs.
rows.anchor: وهو اليهود وأبعدهم الله من رحمته وسخط عليهم بكفرهم وانهماكهم في المعاصي بعد وضوح الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Jews were transformed into apes under David after violating the Sabbath, and some into pigs under Jesus after eating from the table and disbelieving despite clear signs.
rows.anchor: مسخ بعضهم قردة في زمن داود عليه السلام بدعائه عليهم حين اعتدوا في السبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says both transformations affected the Sabbath violators: their young became apes and their elders pigs.
rows.anchor: وقيل كلا المسخين في أصحاب السبت مسخت شبانهم قردة وشيوخهم خنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After revelation, Muslims called the Jews brothers of apes and pigs; the Jews lowered their heads in shame.
rows.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية قال المسلمون لليهود يا إخوة القردة والخنازير فنكسوا رؤوسهم وافتضحوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping the false deity is coordinated with the description of the cursed ones; they obeyed Satan in what he enticed them to do.
rows.anchor: عطف على صلة من وضميره المستكن يعود إلى من أي أطاع الشيطان فيما سول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling their place worse intensifies the description of their wickedness; “farther astray” reinforces “worse.”
rows.anchor: جعل مكانهم شرا ليكون أبلغ في الدلالة على شرارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their religion is wholly evil and distant from truth; the two comparative forms signal absolute excess, not comparison with others who share some evil or error.
rows.anchor: وصيغة التفضيل في الموضعين للزيادة مطلقا لا بالإضافة إلى من يشاركهم في أصل الشرارة والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People tend to love their own group and dislike others, but truth is more deserving of adherence; love among believers is a noble quality.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن كل صنف من الناس يفرح بما لديه ويبغض الآخر بما هو عليه ولكن الحق أحق أن يتبع

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report describes servants who love one another for God alone, without kinship or shared wealth; they will have radiant faces, pulpits of light, and safety from fear and grief.
rows.anchor: قالوا : يا رسول الله أخبرنا من هم وما أعمالهم فلعلنا نحبهم قال : "هم قوم تحابوا في الله على غير أرحام منهم ولا أموال يتعاطون

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الشيرازي
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah al-Shirazi recounts a dream in which the Prophet warned that one who knows God's path, follows it, then turns back will face unparalleled punishment.
rows.anchor: قال أوحد المشايخ في وقته أبو عبد الله الشيرازي قدس سره رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المنام وهو يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is severe because the seeker turned away after recognizing the true path to God; spiritual trials are why seekers retreat, and knowing is not like not knowing.
rows.anchor: إنما كان عذابه أشد لأنه رجع عن طريقه بعد معرفته أنه الحق الموصل إلى الله تعالى وليس من يعلم كمن لا يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawi couplet is cited at the point about the recognized path and the seeker's ordeal; no further gloss is supplied in this passage.
rows.anchor: وسبب الرجوع الامتحانات في الطريق ، قال في "المثنوي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafiz's couplet warns against abandoning the garden path because the seeker cannot bear its thorns, supporting the call to endure hardship.
rows.anchor: فينبغي للطالب الصادق أن يتحمل مشاق الرياضات ويزكي نفسه عن الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sincere seeker should endure ascetic discipline, purify the self of desires, and avoid even lawful food; fasting and eating less are powerful means, though reform ultimately depends on God's grace.
rows.anchor: فينبغي للطالب الصادق أن يتحمل مشاق الرياضات ويزكي نفسه عن الشهوات ويحترز عن أكل ما يجده من الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seeker repeatedly asked his self who it was; only after stricter discipline and reducing food until the ego died did it answer that it had become annihilated.
rows.anchor: فاشتغل أشد من الأول وعالج بتقليل الطعام حتى أمات نفسه

rows.speaker: المولوي
rows.claim: Asked whether a Sufi sins, the Mawlawi replied that eating before appetite is the exception, since such food is poison and illness for him.
rows.anchor: وسئل حضرة المولوي هل يعصي الصوفي قال : لا إلا أن يأكل طعاما قبل الاشتهاء

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa defines game as any wild animal that resists capture, edible or not, except harmful vermin that may be killed in or out of the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: وهو عند أبي حنيفة اسم لكل ممتنع متوحش من الحيوانات سواء كان مأكول اللحم أو لم يكن والمراد ما عدا الفواسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition applies to a pilgrim in ihram even outside Mecca's sanctuary and also to a non-pilgrim inside it; a pilgrim cannot hunt anywhere, while others may hunt outside the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: جمع حرام وهو المحرم وإن كان في الحل وفي حكمه من في الحرم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far gives the sanctuary's distances from its four sides as six, twelve, eighteen, and twenty-four miles.
rows.anchor: ومقداره من قبل المشرق ستة أميال ومن الجانب الثاني اثنا عشر ميلا ومن الجانب الثالث ثمانية عشر ميلا ومن الجانب الرابع أربعة وعشرون ميلا هكذا قال الفقيه أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says killing rather than slaughter to show that game killed by a pilgrim is carrion, not validly slaughtered and therefore inedible.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر القتل دون الذبح للإيذان بكونه في حكم الميتة فكل ما يقتله المحرم من الصيد لا يكون مذكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The game in question is terrestrial, whether edible or not; specifying the offender as a believer rebukes failure to act according to faith.
rows.anchor: الصيد المعهود البري مأكولا كان أو غير مأكول حال كون القاتل كائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deliberate killing means knowing one's ihram and the prohibition; although the verse specifies intention, accidental violations are included as a stricter rule.
rows.anchor: ذاكرا لإحرامه عالما بحرمة قتل ما يقتله والتقييد بالتعمد مع أن محظورات الإحرام يستوي فيها الخطأ والعمد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf measure equivalence by the killed animal's value rather than its shape or kind; the animal is valued where it was killed or nearby if there is no market.
rows.anchor: والمراد به عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف المثل باعتبار القيمة لا باعتبار الخلقة والهيئة فيتقوم الصيد حيث صيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the animal's value reaches that of an offering, the offender may offer an animal of equal value, feed the poor, or fast one day for each poor person's food share.
rows.anchor: فإن بلغت قيمته قيمة هدى تخير الجاني بأن يشتري بها ما قيمته قيمة الصيد فيهديه إلى الحرم وبين أن يشتري بها طعاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each poor person receives half a sa‘ of wheat or a sa‘ of dates; any remainder too small for a full share is donated or covered by one full day of fasting.
rows.anchor: فيعطي كل مسكين نصف صاع من بر أو صاعا من تمر وبين أن يصوم عن طعام كل مسكين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The livestock phrase explains the offering bought at the animal's value; in Arabic it covers camels, cattle, and sheep, though individually only camels are called na‘am.
rows.anchor: فإن فعل ذلك يصدق عليه أنه جزى بمثل ما قتل من النعم والنعم في اللغة من الإبل والبقر والغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two appointed judges are two upright Muslim men.
rows.anchor: بمثل ما قتل صفة لجزاء {ذوا عدل من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An offering is an animal brought to the House in devotion, from a sheep at the least to a camel at the greatest.
rows.anchor: الهدي ما يهدي إلى البيت تقربا إلى الله تعالى من النعم أيسره شاة وأوسطه بقرة وأعلاه بدنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offering is to reach the sanctuary by being slaughtered there; merely giving the matching animal to the sanctuary's poor is insufficient, though Abu Hanifa allows distribution anywhere after slaughter.
rows.anchor: ومعنى بلوغه الكعبة ذبحه بالحرم حتى لو دفع الهدى المماثل للمقتول إلى فقراء الحرم لم يجز بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expiation clause is a second description of the compensation; “food of the poor” explains expiation for grammarians who allow an indefinite noun to be explained by a definite one.
rows.anchor: عطف على محل من النعم على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف والجملة صفة ثانية الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Equivalent of that in fasting” links fasting to the food option and makes equivalence a required measure for the offering, food, or fast.
rows.anchor: عطف على طعام الخ كأنه قيل فعليه جزاء مماثل للمقتول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offering and feeding options apply directly, while fasting follows through the food measure; the offender chooses among the alternatives.
rows.anchor: فيختار الجاني كلا منها بدلا من الآخرين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra distinguishes kasra ʿadl, an equivalent of the same kind, from fatha ʿadl, an equivalent of another kind or one matched in measure; their forms reflect source and passive-participle senses.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء العدل بالكسر المثل من جنسه والعدل بالفتح المثل من غير جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “that” points to food, fasting is an accusative of specification, and Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf give the choice to the offender while Muhammad gives it to the judges.
rows.anchor: وذلك إشارة إلى الطعام وصياما تمييز للعدل والخيار في ذلك للجاني عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف وللحكمين عند محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The penalty is imposed so the game killer tastes the bad consequence of violating ihram; wabal is harm or an unpleasant outcome that follows from an act urged by the self.
rows.anchor: سوء عاقبة هتكه لحرمة الإحرام والوبال في الأصل المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God pardoned what passed” refers to game killed in ihram before the prohibition was revealed.
rows.anchor: من قتل الصيد محرما قبل التحريم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say a person who repeats the prohibited killing owes another expiation; others say no expiation is due on recurrence, relying on the verse's apparent wording.
rows.anchor: وأما الكفارة فعن بعضهم أنها واجبة على العائد وعن بعضهم أنه لا كفارة عليه تعلقا بالظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vengeance clause means God punishes the returning offender in the afterlife; an implicit subject is supplied so the conditional fa has a grammatical function.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالانتقام التعذيب في الآخرة وأما الكفارة فعن بعضهم أنها واجبة على العائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vengeance originally means victory or requital; when ascribed to God it means punishment and recompense, and God is overpowering and severe toward persistent transgressors.
rows.anchor: وأصل الانتقام الانتصار والانتصاف وإذا أضيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying addressed to Abraham warns that God carries out His decree without distinction among prophet, saint, or enemy, as a fierce lion attacks without distinguishing helpful from harmful prey.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى مخاطبا لخليله (يا إبراهيم خف مني كما تخاف من السبع الضاري)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should avoid disobedience as far as possible because they reap what they sow; the Mathnawi couplet is cited to reinforce this warning.
rows.anchor: فليحذر العاقل من المخالفة والعصيان بقدر الاستطاعة والإمكان أينما كان فإن الإنسان لا يحصد إلا ما يزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak people disobey the mighty God through immersion in desires and heedlessness of Him.
rows.anchor: والعجب أن الإنسان الضعيف كيف يعصي الله القوي وليس إلا من الانهماك في الشهوات والغفلة عن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, worldly people who settle for bodily worship may hunt, while lovers in the state of renouncing the world to visit union's Kaaba must abstain from worldly prey.
rows.anchor: أباح الصيد لمن كان حلالا وهم أهل السلو من العوام الذين رضوا من الكمالات الدينية بالأعمال البدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker of God must sever all greed and seek only union; the gnostic is God's prey, so the prey itself cannot hunt.
rows.anchor: من قصدنا فعليه بحسم الاطماع جملة ولا ينبغي أن يكون له مطالبة بحال من الأحوال إلا طلب الوصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When seekers deliberately turn toward something worldly despite knowing its harm, the matching recompense is ascetic discipline and struggle whose pain balances the pleasure of desire.
rows.anchor: إذا التفت لشيء من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two just judges inwardly are heart and spirit; by the measure of faith they prescribe less food and drink, giving wealth, leaving sexual activity, solitude, retreat, and control of the senses.
rows.anchor: وهو القلب والروح يحكمان على مقدار الإيمان وعلى أنواع الرياضات بتقليل الطعام والشراب أو ببذل المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching the Kaaba inwardly means acting with pure sincerity fit to receive the Real without regard for people.
rows.anchor: أي خالصاتعالى فيما يعمل بحيث يصلح لقبول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inwardly needy faculties are intellect, heart, secret, spirit, and hidden self; they need spiritual nourishment through sincere focus, turning from creation, patience, detachment, gratitude, contentment, and submission.
rows.anchor: وهم العقل والقلب والسر والروح والخفي فإنهم كانوا محرمين من أغذيتهم الروحانية من صدق التوجه إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inward fasting means ceasing to notice otherness, demand personal choice, or rely on anything besides the Almighty King.
rows.anchor: والصيام هو الإمساك عن ملاحظة الأغيار وطلب الاختيار والركون إلى غير الملك الجبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lower self tastes the harm of disciplines that oppose its nature as recompense and expiation for the pleasures of desire and heedlessness.
rows.anchor: أي : تتألم بألم هذه المعاملات التي على خلاف طبعها جزاء وكفارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God pardons what seekers did before they began the spiritual quest; returning to worldly attachment afterward brings abandonment here and loss in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: إلى تعلق شيء من الدنيا بعد الخروج عنها بقدم الصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For lovers, divine vengeance is a veil of majesty proportionate to their attention to anything besides God; enemies are punished by the turning of their hearts and eyes.
rows.anchor: ينتقم من أحبائه باحتجاب التعزز بالكبرياء والعظمة على قدر التفاتهم إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited Hafez couplet longs for the return of people to their former ordered condition; the author glosses it as a return to the state they had been in.
rows.anchor: أي : كالوضع الذي كانوا عليه من الانتظام مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question presses Meccans to admit that all rational and non-rational things in heaven and earth belong to God by creation, ownership, and control.
rows.anchor: إلجاء لأهل مكة إلى الإقرار بأن الكل من العقلاء وغيرهمخلقا وملكا وتصرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the answer is self-evident, the questioner answers before others; the passage hints that no answer should be awaited before confessing it.
rows.anchor: وفي تصدي السائل للجواب قبل أن يجيب غيره إيماء إلى أن مثل هذا السؤال لكون جوابه متعينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's self-imposed mercy means He graciously undertook it, delays punishment, and accepts repentance; nothing is truly obligatory upon Him.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كتب الرحمة على نفسه التزمها وأوجبها تفضلا وإحسانا لأنه تعالى منزه عن أن يجب عليه شيء حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “Himself” is evidence against those who deny that the word nafs may be used of God.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير عن الذات بالنفس حجة على من ادعى أن لفظ النفس لا يطلق على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implicit oath answers that God will surely raise or gather people from their graves for judgment on their polytheism and sins, despite having spared them worldly punishment through mercy.
rows.anchor: والله ليجمعكم في القبور مبعوثين أو محشورين إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There is no doubt” may refer to the Day of Resurrection alone or to the whole preceding statement.
rows.anchor: في اليوم أو في الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who lose themselves squander their original capital: innate disposition and sound reason; their refusal to believe follows from this loss.
rows.anchor: بتضييع رأس مالهم وهو الفطرة الأصلية والعقل السليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following senses and conjecture, blind imitation, and neglecting reflection disables reason, entrenches disbelief, and removes people from special mercy.
rows.anchor: فإن إبطال العقل باتباع الحواس والوهم والانهماك في التقليد وإغفال النظر أدى بهم إلى الإصرار على الكفر

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says mercy encompasses both worlds, including guidance to know God and His oneness through proofs, revealed books, and respite for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: القاضي : والمراد بالرحمة ما يعم الدارين ومن ذلك الهداية إلى معرفته

rows.speaker: تفسير الكاشفي
rows.claim: The Kashifi commentary identifies this as God's essential, all-encompassing mercy, whose first gift is bestowed without prior request, need, or deserving claim.
rows.anchor: وفي "تفسير الكاشفي" : (مراد رحمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Mathnawi couplet supports the claim that people had no prior claim to existence, life, or knowledge; God's grace hears even an unspoken need.
rows.anchor: ما نبوديم وتقاضا مان نبود لطف تونا كفته ما مى شنود

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying God kept ninety-nine of one hundred parts of mercy and sent one to earth, from which creatures show mercy, even a mare lifting its hoof for its foal.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This report gives Muslims great hope: one part already accounts for the world's outward and inward blessings, so the hundred parts in the next world promise far more.
rows.anchor: فهذا مما يدل على كمال الرجاء والبشارة للمسلمين لأنه حصل في هذه الدار من رحمة واحدة ما حصل من النعم

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar reports that the Prophet compared God's mercy for His servants to a mother who would never cast her nursing child into fire.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال : قدم على النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You forget your partners” means wholly abandoning the idols, since reason recognizes that only God can remove affliction; forget here means leave, not become heedless.
rows.anchor: أي تتركون ما تشركون به تعالى من الأصنام تركا كليا لما ركز في العقول إنه القادر على كشف العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that messengers were sent is an oath: by God, messengers were indeed sent.
rows.anchor: أي : وبالله لقد أرسلنا رسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers went to many communities before Muhammad's time; the Kufan grammatical view takes min as marking the beginning of a time span.
rows.anchor: كائنة من زمان قبل زمانك فمن لابتداء الغاية في الزمان على مذهب الكوفية

rows.speaker: سنان لبي
rows.claim: Sinaan Labi says min is an augmentative particle for those who allow it in affirmative clauses; others take it to mean “in,” as in the Friday prayer verse.
rows.anchor: سنان لبي : من زائدة على قول من جوز زيادتها في الموجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in “so We seized them” fills an omitted link: they rejected their messengers, so God seized them.
rows.anchor: الفاء فصيحة تفصح أن الكلام مبني على اعتبار الحذف أي فكذبوا رسلهم فأخذناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ba'sa' means hardship and poverty; al-darra' means harm and afflictions, and both are feminine forms without masculine counterparts.
rows.anchor: أي بالشدة والفقر {والضرآء} أي : الضر والآفات وهما صيغتا تأنيث لا مذكر لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of afflicting them was that they might humbly pray for relief and repent their disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: أي لكي يدعو الله في كشفها بالتضرع والتذلل ويتوبوا إليه من كفرهم ومعاصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse begins the rebuke that they did not implore when God's punishment came.
rows.anchor: هلا {إذ جآءهم بأسنآ} عذابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They failed to implore despite the reason to do so; la-wla conveys blame and regret when a motive to act exists and no excuse remains.
rows.anchor: لم يفعلوا ذلك مع قيام المقتضى له فلولا يفيد اللوم والتنديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts instead hardened and dried; if their hearts had been tender and fearful, they would have implored.
rows.anchor: استدراك على المعنى أي لم يتضرعوا ولكن يبست وجفت قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan made disbelief and sins seem attractive by luring them toward pleasure and ease rather than reflection; they failed to see their affliction was caused by their own conduct.
rows.anchor: حسن لهم الكفر والمعاصي بأن أغواهم ودعاهم إلى اللذة والراحة دون التفكر والتدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax implies that they became absorbed in wrongdoing and forgot the warnings conveyed through hardship before God opened blessings to them.
rows.anchor: عطف على مقدر أي فانهمكوا فيه ونسوا ما ذكروا به من البأساء والضراء فلما نسوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God opened every kind of blessing to them as a form of gradual entrapment, or istidraj.
rows.anchor: من فنون النعماء على مناهج الاستدراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their joy was arrogant self-satisfaction with what they received, like Qarun's delight in worldly wealth.
rows.anchor: فالفرح فرح البطر كفرح قارون بما أصابه من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were struck suddenly so the blow would be more forceful; scholars of rhetoric say catching them in comfort made regret for lost safety and well-being even sharper.
rows.anchor: أي : فجأة ليكون أشد عليهم وقعا وأفظع هولا كما قال أهل المعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were left in utter regret and despair, with no hope of escape; fa-idha marks surprise and iblas means losing hope of salvation at calamity.
rows.anchor: متحسرون غاية الحسرة آيسون من كل خير راجون فإذا للمفاجأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dābir of the wrongdoers means their last remnant, so not one remained; the word denotes a follower behind, as a child follows a parent.
rows.anchor: آخرهم بحيث لم يبق منهم أحد فالدابر يقال للتابع للشيء من خلفه

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says punishment eradicated them completely; calling them wrongdoers instead of using a pronoun identifies the cause as their injustice, putting disbelief for gratitude and sins for obedience.
rows.anchor: البغوي : معناه إنهم استؤصلوا بالعذاب فلم يبق منهم باقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise is due for their destruction because removing the harm of corrupt beliefs and deeds is a great blessing, especially when it elevates the truth voiced by their messengers.
rows.anchor: فإن هلاك الكفار والعصاة من حيث إنه تخليص لأهل العرض من شؤم عقائدهم الفاسدة وأعمالهم الخبيثة نعمة جليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the refuge in ease and hardship; everything else is only a means, while God alone truly acts. A believer turns to Him willingly in every state, unlike a disbeliever who turns only in crisis.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى هو المرجع في كل أمر حال الاختيار والاضطرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alternates hardship and comfort like a caring father who disciplines and caresses a child to reform him, establish the proof, and remove excuses; this can benefit worldly and religious life if recognized.
rows.anchor: يقلب الإنسان تارة من البأساء والضراء إلى الراحة والرخاء وأنواع الآلاء والنعماء وأخرى يعكس الأمر كما يفعله الأب المشفق بولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A couplet by al-Sa'ib compares a hard nature to a surface that reason cannot polish, while all conditions of time can serve as a whetstone.
rows.anchor: ففي هذه المعاملة تربية له وفائدة عظيمة في دينه ودنياه إن تفطن : قال الصائب (من) :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destruction can be part of gradual entrapment; a Prophetic report says that when God gives a sinner what he loves, it may be istidraj, then recites the verse about forgetting the warning.
rows.anchor: إذا رأيت الله تعالى يعطي عبدا في الدنيا على معصية ما يحب فإن ذلك منه استدراج
